PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

MEMORANDUM
TO: Lena Fischbach, COO; Jared Polk, VP Customer Experience
FROM: Office of the General Counsel (draft for Miranda Solano)
RE: FLSA/State Exempt Classification - Customer Experience & Analytics Specialist (CEAS), 18 positions (Austin 8, Irvine 6, Portland 4)
Note: the file ends March 2025; this memo applies law as of October 2, 2026. If CEAS employees are already working as exempt, see Part VIII item 5.

I. BOTTOM LINE
1. Classify all 18 CEAS positions as NON-EXEMPT, with timekeeping, as written. Do not adopt Thornbury's "Exempt - Administrative" recommendation.
2. Irvine (6): the exemption is unavailable on two independent grounds. (a) Salary: $55,200 is below California's exempt floor ($68,640 in 2025; $70,304 from Jan. 1, 2026). (b) Duties: California requires more than 50% of actual time on exempt work; at most 25% of this role is even arguably exempt. Either ground alone defeats exemption. This is not a close call.
3. Austin (8) and Portland (4): the salary level is satisfied, but the duties test is most likely failed. The administrative primary duty is customer service/CRM work (roughly 60-75% of time), which is production/front-line work, and the arguably exempt analytics work is 25% of time and largely template-driven. Exempt classification is unlikely to be defensible, and, given the record, would carry willfulness risk.
4. A single national classification is also the practical answer: one job description, one FLSA status, pay-equity consistency, and no 18-person misclassification class.

II. FACTS
CEAS merges the eliminated Customer Insights Analyst (exempt, $72,000) and Senior CSR (non-exempt, $24.50/hr) into one Grade 7 role at $55,200 flat salary ($26.54/hr on 40 hours; band $50,000-$62,000); no supervision; reports to a non-exempt Team Lead. Job description time split: 40% scripted customer service (Tier 1/2; Tier 3 escalated); 20% CRM entry and pre-built reports; 25% Tableau analysis using "established templates" and "standardized report formats," flagging NPS deviations to the Team Lead; 15% upselling per an "Upsell Playbook" with targets. Mr. Polk's emails call the role "primarily customer-facing" and the service/data entry "table stakes." Ms. Fischbach (Feb. 12) and Ms. Solano (Mar. 28) flagged California salary, the duties test and willfulness. The grid lists CEAS as exempt with blank California/Oregon notes.

III. SOURCES AND HIERARCHY OF AUTHORITY
Binding: FLSA, 29 U.S.C. 207(a), 213(a)(1), 255, 260, 216(b); 29 C.F.R. Part 541; U.S. Supreme Court and Fifth Circuit decisions (Texas); Ninth Circuit for Oregon/California federal-law issues (persuasive in state-law questions); California Labor Code 515, 510, 226.7, 203, 2698 et seq.; IWC Wage Order 4-2001 (8 CCR 11040); Oregon ORS ch. 652-653 and OAR 839-020. Persuasive/non-binding: DOL Fact Sheets and opinion letters, and the Thornbury letter (a consultant opinion, expressly "not legal advice").

IV. FEDERAL ANALYSIS
A. Salary level - Thornbury is wrong about the rule in force, but the result is the same. Thornbury relied on the 2024 DOL rule ($844/wk effective July 1, 2024; $1,128/wk Jan. 1, 2025). On Nov. 15, 2024 the E.D. Tex. vacated that rule nationwide (State of Texas v. U.S. Dep't of Labor, No. 4:24-cv-499 (E.D. Tex.)); the threshold reverted to $684/wk ($35,568), and the appeal ended in dismissal in 2026 with DOL formally restoring the 2019 levels (reported May 2026; confirm in the Federal Register). The grid's "$844/wk" entries and "Federal Salary Threshold Met? Yes - exceeds $844" are stale and should be corrected. Salary of $55,200 clears either figure, so salary level is satisfied federally. Salary basis (29 C.F.R. 541.602) is satisfied only if pay is not docked for quality/quantity of work; note Helix Energy Solutions Group v. Hewitt, 598 U.S. 39 (2023) (daily-rate pay does not meet salary basis for highly paid non-salary workers; salary basis rules remain strictly applied).

B. Duties test, 29 C.F.R. 541.200. The employer bears the burden, with a "fair reading" of exemptions (Encino Motorcars, LLC v. Navarro, 584 U.S. 79 (2018)).
1. Primary duty (541.700): the principal, main, major or most important duty; over 50% of time on exempt work is a guidepost, but less can suffice if relative importance, freedom from supervision and pay support it. Only 25% is analytics; 75% is service, data entry and sales. Supervision is heavy (scripts, playbook, scorecards, templates, Team Lead review). Pay ($55,200) is far below the eliminated analyst's $72,000 and near the old CSR's (about $50,960). Thornbury's "integrated whole" theory, treating 40% service as incidental, is contradicted by the job description and Mr. Polk's own emails.
2. Prong 1 (541.201): administrative work services the business, as distinguished from production of its goods and services (541.201(a)). Answering inquiries, processing returns, resolving complaints and upselling is front-line service and sales. See Dewan v. M-I, L.L.C., 858 F.3d 331 (5th Cir. 2017); Hobbs v. EVO Inc., 7 F.4th 241 (5th Cir. 2021) (actual duties control). Data entry and running pre-built dashboards are not exempt work.
3. Prong 2 (541.202): requires comparing and evaluating courses of conduct and acting with authority free from immediate direction; applying procedures or skills does not qualify (541.202(e)). Tier 1/2 is scripted, Tier 3 escalated, upsell playbook-driven, reports template-based, NPS issues flagged upward; no authority over policy. Thornbury's account (custom dashboards, metric selection, recommendations) does not match the job description it analyzed, and Thornbury admits it did not observe the work.
4. Other exemptions fail: executive (no supervision), learned professional (no degree requirement), computer employee (end-user Tableau), outside sales (JD bars outside sales); combination (541.708) cannot rescue 75% non-exempt time.

C. Internal precedent. The 2022 Ridgewater & Calloway memo reached non-exempt status for the Marketing Coordinator ($54,000) with 85% production, template-driven duties and only 15% brainstorming. CEAS is not identical (CEAS has 25% analytics), but the same reasoning applies: template-driven work, supervisory review, end-user reporting. The memo is privileged; it is not binding on any court, and treating it as controlling overstates it. But it is highly relevant as notice: it warned the Company that hybrid roles require counsel review, that consultant recommendations are not legal analysis, and that proceeding over counsel's contrary advice supports willfulness (McLaughlin v. Richland Shoe Co., 486 U.S. 128, 133 (1988)). Do not circulate the memo outside Legal (waiver risk); use it internally and describe conclusions in the privileged advice.

V. CALIFORNIA (Irvine, 6 employees) - exemption unavailable
1. Salary. Cal. Lab. Code 515(a) and Wage Order 4-2001, 1(A)(2)(g): exempt administrative employees must earn a monthly salary of at least two times the state minimum wage for full-time work. 2025: $16.50 x 2 x 2,080 = $68,640. 2026: $16.90 x 2 x 2,080 = $70,304. $55,200 is short by $13,440 (2025) and $15,104 (2026). The Thornbury letter does not address California at all (it says to ask counsel); Mr. Polk's statement that Thornbury "accounted for the geographic piece" is unsupported by the letter. The grid's California threshold note for Grade 7 CEAS is blank while Grade 8 shows $68,640. Note that the Grade 7 maximum ($62,000) is below the threshold, so no one in Grade 7 could be exempt in California.
2. Duties. Wage Order 4 requires that the employee be "primarily engaged" in exempt duties, i.e., more than half of working time (Lab. Code 515(e)); the test is quantitative, plus the employer must show customarily and regularly exercised discretion and independent judgment, and work related to management policies or general business operations (not production). California courts apply the "realistic requirements" test of actual work (Ramirez v. Yosemite Water Co., 20 Cal.4th 785 (1999)) and the administrative/production dichotomy (Harris v. Superior Court, 53 Cal.4th 170 (2011); Eicher v. Advance Business Integrators, Inc., 151 Cal.App.4th 1363 (2007)). With at most 25% in arguably exempt analytics, the more-than-50% test fails by a wide margin.
3. Consequences if misclassified. Daily overtime (over 8 hours/day, double time over 12; seventh-day rules) under Lab. Code 510; meal/rest period premiums (226.7); itemized wage statements (226); waiting-time penalties up to 30 days' wages (203); PAGA civil penalties (Lab. Code 2698 et seq.; note the 2024 PAGA reforms changed penalty structure and cure provisions, verify current text); a 3-year (UCL four-year) limitations period for wage claims. Non-exempt status also requires timekeeping and compliant meal/rest breaks and, for the weekend/peak shifts, premium pay; fluctuating-workweek and salary-for-OT arrangements are not permitted. Pay for Irvine non-exempt CEAS must meet Irvine/state minimum and any local rule.

VI. OREGON (Portland remote, 4 employees)
Remote work does not change the governing law; Oregon wage-hour law applies to employees working in Oregon. ORS 653.020(3) exempts administrative employees only if they perform predominantly intellectual, managerial or creative tasks, exercise discretion and independent judgment, and are paid on a salary basis at or above the statutory floor (applicable regional minimum wage x 2,080 hours; OAR 839-020-0005 et seq.). At the Portland metro rate in the grid ($15.95/hr) the floor is about $33,176 (rises each July 1; verify the current rate), so $55,200 clears it, but the duties analysis tracks the federal analysis and fails for the same reasons ("predominantly intellectual" is not met by scripted service and data entry). The grid's statement that Oregon "follows federal FLSA" is incomplete; Oregon applies its own statute and BOLI rules, and these must be reviewed. I did not independently verify the current Oregon figures or BOLI duties rules; Oregon counsel or BOLI guidance should confirm before finalizing. Oregon requires overtime over 40 hours/week and provides rest and meal period rules (OAR 839-020-0050); the remote work setting also requires accurate timekeeping of off-site hours and employer-provided equipment/expense considerations.

VII. WILLFULNESS AND EXPOSURE
- FLSA: back overtime at 1.5x; 2 years, 3 years if willful (29 U.S.C. 255(a)); liquidated (double) damages unless the employer proves good faith and reasonable grounds (29 U.S.C. 260); fees (216(b)). Willful = knew or showed reckless disregard (Richland Shoe).
- Record: the COO flagged California and duties in February; the GC flagged both on March 28 with willfulness. Proceeding on a consultant's non-legal letter that skips California and concedes it is not legal advice would likely forfeit a good-faith defense and could prove reckless disregard, notwithstanding the 2022 memo's warning. Reliance on legal advice supports good faith; deliberate disregard of it destroys it. Do not rely on Thornbury as a defense.
VIII. RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Classify all 18 as non-exempt (hourly, timekeeping). Convert the job description's FLSA field to "Non-Exempt," change the grid (v3.2) FLSA/threshold entries, update the stale $844/$1,128 references, and complete the California and Oregon notes. Do not post as exempt.
2. Pay: hourly rate at or above $26.54 equivalent (or lower the band consistent with the CSR-level role) with overtime budgeted; California daily overtime rules built into payroll (Lone Star Payroll); meal/rest compliance for Irvine; recordkeeping per 29 C.F.R. Part 516.
3. Alternative if the business wants exempt analysts: re-scope to a genuine analyst role (separate from service/CRM/sales) with a majority of time on independent analysis, authority over metric selection and recommendations, salary above $70,304 (California) and at least the Oregon floor, and obtain a duties analysis by counsel from actual incumbent observation. That is a different job.
4. Direct Thornbury through counsel only; obtain a written engagement correction (its letter is wrong on the rule in force and silent on California/Oregon); keep this memo privileged and limit distribution.
5. If any CEAS have already worked as exempt: reclassify prospectively now, quantify and pay back overtime for all hours with counsel (consider counsel-supervised self-audit; FLSA releases require DOL supervision or court approval in most cases; California rights are non-waivable), and preserve documents.
6. Adopt a hybrid-role review protocol: counsel signoff before any exempt coding, annual reviews, and time-study of actual duties 6 months after launch.

IX. CAVEATS
Facts rest on the draft JD, not observed duties. Discrepancies to reconcile: Thornbury says the Board approved the restructuring, the JD says the COO; emails use a crestviewoutdoor.com domain; the grid puts Marketing Coordinator and CEAS in one exempt Grade 7 row despite the 2022 reclassification. I did not fetch full text of every case; confirm pin cites and current Oregon and 2026 California figures before external use.
